newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria forex reserves rise to $1.09 bln April 21.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria forex reserves rise to $1.09 bln April 21.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Monday its foreign exchange reserves rose to $1.09 billion on April 21 from $554.3 million on March 31.
BNB FX RESERVES APRIL 21 MARCH APRIL'96
"Under current estimates reserves amount to $1.09 billion after Bulgaria received $150 million from the sale of (soda ash producer) Sodi Devnya at the end of last week", the BNB said in a statement.
The rise was also due to BNB net dollar purchases and $178.7 million of International Monetary Fund (IMF) loans received under a funding package approved this month, a BNB official told Reuters.

Of the $178.7 million received in BNB accounts, $31.7 million were the first tranche of a $510 million standby credit, while $147 million were the Compensatory and Contingency Financing Facility (CCFF).

The IMF approved on April 11 the 14-month standby credit to enable Bulgaria to carry out reforms including introduction of a currency board, a self-regulating monetary mechanism designed to halt inflation and stabilise the lev currency.
The CCFF loan was extended to fund grain imports to offset acute wheat shortages caused by uncontrolled exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year.

Last week, Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay SA had finalised its purchase of 60 percent of soda ash producer Sodi for a total of $160 million, Bulgaria's biggest sell-off so far.

Under the contract, Solvay has agreed to invest $67 million over the next five years on increasing dense soda ash capacity from 400,000 tonnes a year at present, and on modernisation and environmental improvements.
Apart from foreign exchange reserves, the BNB held monetary gold reserves of 32.074 tonnes, or about 1.03 million troy ounces in its vaults at end-March.
